## Dev workflow

The Agentic Framework drives everything through `ag` commands. The CLI enforces
the workflow — never skip steps.

| Step | Command | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Where am I? | `ag status` | Current work items + suggested next step |
| Pick up work | `ag start F-XXXX "Title"` | New feature; CLI checks artifacts |
| Plan first | `ag plan F-XXXX` | Drafts a plan; review before code |
| Implement | `ag implement F-XXXX` | Spawns a worktree; auto-creates AGENTS.json entry |
| Commit | `ag commit` | Runs Tier 0 gates; never use `git commit --no-verify` |
| Push | `ag push` | Pre-push gate: full tests + drift + coverage |
| Done | `ag done F-XXXX` | VERSION bump, doc gate, state flush |

If any gate blocks you, the error message names a concrete next-step command
(R-012 catalog). Read it before retrying.

## Make your first commit (5 minutes)

This walkthrough writes a journal entry — a low-stakes change that exercises
the full commit pipeline so you can confirm hooks/integrity/tests are wired.

```bash
# 1. Append a journal entry recording your onboarding.
bash .agentic/lib/tools/journal.sh \
    "Onboarding $(whoami)" \
    "Cloned the repo and ran ag onboard." \
    "Read STACK.md and one ADR, then pick up a task" \
    "—" \
    --why "Confirming local hooks fire and the journal is wired."

# 2. Stage + commit through the gate. State-only commits skip tests, so this
#    will pass even before you've configured a test runner locally.
git add .agentic/journal/JOURNAL.md
ag commit
```

If the commit succeeds, your hooks are healthy. If it fails, the gate output
points at the fix — the most common is `INTEGRITY_TAMPERED`, which means
hooks need re-installing: `ag hooks register` (R-015) or `ag integrity update`
to acknowledge an intentional change.
